From: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: PrivDeploy module gating and network ops review

Hi team,

I'm opening a focused review thread for the private deployment IaC changes we need to gate this quarter. Attached is a condensed patch with the Terraform module changes, the proposed Helm value override patterns, and an initial GitLab CI snippet to run preflight checks. High-level ask: can we sign off on the module gating checklist and CI tests so we can schedule the on-prem rollout for Acme Corp the week of 12/14?

Quick points to consider while reviewing:
- Terraform module: new aws_vpc/private_subnet module extracted, new variables for network CIDR pools and allocation strategy.
- Helm: adds an optional nodeSelector/taint-aware profile for air-gapped clusters.
- Ansible: bootstrapping role for bastion + CA ingestion.
- CI: pipeline job should run tfplan, helm lint/diff, static security checks, and a network preflight that calls the vNet validator.

Please annotate the patch with any blocking security or networking items. I want named owners on the checklist by EOD Thu.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:03:12 -0800
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy module gating and network ops review

Thanks Kim — quick pass below. I pulled the patch into a feature branch and ran tfplan against the Acme staging account. Highlights and immediate concerns:

1) TF module behavior: the private_subnet module now supports explicit allocation pools (start/end) which is good. We need to add an assertion that prevents overlapping allocations when multiple clusters are deployed in the same account. Suggested: add a data lookup that checks for existing subnets with the same allocation tag and fail the plan if overlap detected.

2) KMS + key policies: ensure the module accepts an external KMS key id (optional) and does not create a cross-account key by default — many customers require customer-managed keys.

3) CI gating: the gitlab snippet works but we should add a network e2e job that executes from a sandbox VM inside the VPC to validate routing to the customer's peering endpoint and tests DNS resolution for private-records. This should run after 'helm diff' but before applying.

4) Helm: for the taint-aware profile, confirm the toleration strategy for system pods (metrics/proxy) — we should default system pods to run on control-plane-exempt nodes.

I'll attach a small pipeline snippet that wires tfsec and the sandbox e2e runner. I can own adding the overlap assertion and the e2e job.

-dev

Attachments: gitlab-ci-privdeploy-snippet.yml (ci snippet)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 08:22:45 -0800
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy module gating and network ops review

Appreciate the pace here. A couple of security + compliance items that need explicit confirmation before we greenlight: 

- Audit logging: the module must enable flow logs to a customer-managed S3 bucket and produce CloudTrail events for ENI allocations. Add policy templates for log retention and an optional role for cross-account log delivery.
- Private CA: the Ansible role references 'ingest CA cert' but we need automated validation of the chain and a rotation plan. Recommend adding an acceptance test that performs an mTLS handshake with the service endpoint using the new cert.
- IPAM governance: the allocation strategy should support both centralized IPAM (managed by customer) and delegated mode. Add an explicit variable 'ipam_mode' with values [delegated, managed] and document the operational implications in Confluence.

Also, file INFRA-1428 for tracking the audit evidence we need for Acme's SOC review (I've linked the ticket). Hannah, can you scope the log retention/role template work? Kim, can you confirm the acceptance test expectations for the CA rotation?

-Marissa
VP, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Related: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-1428

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Marissa — thanks. Action items and owners below, I took liberty to assign tentative owners so we can move quickly: 

- Dev: add IP overlap assertion and network e2e job in GitLab (owner: dev_patel) — target: 12/07
- Security: log templates + cross-account delivery role + retention policy (owner: hannah_schmitt) — target: 12/09
- Kim: acceptance test for CA ingestion and rotation; define steps & pass/fail criteria — target: 12/08
- Marissa: confirm policy language for KMS external key usage and sign-off on audit evidence list — target: 12/06

For rollout gating: we will require the following CI green checkmarks before a merge to release branch: tfplan-no-overlap, tfsec-severity<=medium, helm-diff-no-changes-to-system, network-e2e-passed, ca-acceptance-pass. The GitLab MR will be configured to block merge until those conditions are met.

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync Thu morning to review the updated pipeline and the topology diagram (attached).

-Kim

Hi team,

Pushing the first pass of the GitLab CI snippet to the feature MR: https://git.redwood.com/infra/priv-deploy/-/merge_requests/287

Key points in the snippet (attachment gitlab-ci-privdeploy-snippet.yml):
- network-e2e: boots a sandbox VM in the target VPC using an ephemeral TF workspace, runs curl/dig tests against the peered endpoint, and tears down the VM.
- tf-overlap-check: uses awscli to list subnets with metadata tag 'cluster:acme' and fails if ranges intersect.
- parallel stage ordering: plan -> tf-overlap-check -> tfsec -> helm-diff -> network-e2e -> apply-gated

I'll run the snippet in the staging account this afternoon and post logs. If everyone is happy, I'll add the required blocking rules on the MR.

-dev

From: markus.networks@edgecloud.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 04 Dec 2026 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy module gating and network ops review

Kim/Dev,

We pulled the topology and the TF feature branch into the EdgeCloud staging lab and validated peering behavior. A couple of operational notes from the partner side: 

- BGP constraints: we can accept the proposed ASN but require that keepalive is set to 30s and the hold-time not less than 90s; we will advertise only the /24s per our policy.
- MTU: ensure fragment sizes account for our overlay (we recommend 1400).
- DNS: we'll terminate private DNS for the peered zones; add a conditional in the Helm chart so DNS overrides are only applied when 'external_dns: enabled' is true.

We're good to proceed once the e2e sandbox confirms routing (happy to run the e2e runner on our side if helpful). I'll update the MR comments with our peering config and a small patch to the helm values.

-Markus
Network Architect
EdgeCloud (partner)
